title: Affine sections of the conormal sheaf
statement: Let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion] with ideal sheaf $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. If $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq X$ is affine [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $Z\cap U=\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$ for an ideal $I\subseteq R$, then the conormal sheaf $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=i^*\mathcal I$ [def-pc-module-pullback] is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent] and there is a canonical identification $\Gamma(Z\cap U,\mathcal C_{Z/X})\cong I/I^2$, where $I^2$ is the ideal generated by products of two elements of $I$.

source.place: Morphisms, Definition 01R2 (definition-conormal-sheaf), quasi-coherence, and Lemma 01R3 (lemma-affine-conormal), assertion (2) and its proof

proof.text: The ideal module i.ker.toModules is the kernel of the structure-module map to the pushforward from its closed subscheme. The structure modules are quasi-coherent; closed-immersion pushforward and quasi-coherent kernels prove quasi-coherence of the ideal module.

The tensor-pullback adjunction and the usual pullback-pushforward adjunction have the same right adjoint. Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies their functors. Transport quasi-coherence of the usual pullback across this isomorphism to close the first conjunct.
Apply the strictly smaller affine sections equivalence theorem for the second conjunct and combine the two conjuncts. The remaining hole is only this affine identification, not quasi-coherence.

proof_origin.place: Definition 01R2 and Lemma 01R3 (2); quasi-coherence proved using the existing ideal-kernel and pullback results, affine identification isolated as a proper component.
